NORTHWIND INSTRUMENTS (FIXTURE) FORM 10-K FOR THE FISCAL YEAR ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2025

Item 1. Business

Northwind Instruments designs, manufactures and sells analytical instruments, consumables and services to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, academic and government laboratories. Consumables and services represented 61% of total revenue in fiscal 2025, compared with 58% in fiscal 2024. Our installed base exceeded 42,000 instruments at the end of fiscal 2025.

We purchase certain detector components from a single supplier. Three suppliers accounted for approximately 34% of our direct material purchases in fiscal 2025. A disruption at any of these suppliers could delay shipments.

Academic and government customers accounted for 18% of revenue in fiscal 2025. Reductions in research funding could reduce demand for our instruments.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Revenue increased 9% to $2,412 million in fiscal 2025, driven by consumables growth in the pharmaceutical end market. Instrument revenue was flat as customers delayed capital purchases.

Our effective tax rate differs from the U.S. federal statutory income tax rate of 21% mainly because of foreign earnings and research credits.

We have not paid cash dividends on our common stock and do not plan to in the foreseeable future.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

Free cash flow was $468 million in fiscal 2025, compared with $431 million in fiscal 2024. We define free cash flow as cash from operations less capital expenditures.

Contractual obligations (In millions)
Senior notes due 2027 400
Senior notes due 2030 750
Total debt 1,150

Scheduled principal payments over the next five fiscal years total $400 million. We have a $500 million revolving credit facility that expires in 2028, with no amounts drawn as of September 30, 2025.
